script.title: Offer vs Invitation to Offer
script.caption_hook: Is a price tag really an offer? Most people get this wrong.

lines.say: Wait, a shirt with a price tag isn't actually an offer?
Right. An offer can be accepted to make a contract. An invitation only asks people to make offers.
So what's the shop doing with the price tag then?
The shop only invites you. You bring the shirt to the counter. That's your offer, and the shopkeeper accepts.
Okay. What about catalogues and price lists?
Same thing. A catalogue, a price list, a tender notice and an auctioneer's call all only invite offers.
Then where's the real offer in an auction?
Each bid is an offer. The auctioneer accepts it for the seller when the hammer falls.
And a reward advertisement? Is that also just an invitation?
No. A reward promised to anyone who performs a condition is a general offer. The case is Carlill versus Carbolic Smoke Ball Company.
Got it! Window shows, bidder offers.
Perfect. Remember that line. The reward advertisement is the one exception.

check_notes: Writer: Line 8 now says the auctioneer accepts for the seller when the hammer falls (Sale of Goods Act, s.64); the board shows Bidder to Hammer, so no conflicting 'Seller' label. Word count about 165.

Checker: Line 2 (voice): 'An offer can be accepted to make a contract' skips a step. Under Section 2(b) of the Indian Contract Act, an accepted proposal becomes a promise or agreement. It becomes a contract only if it is enforceable by law (Section 2(h), Section 10). Suggested wording: 'An offer, once accepted, becomes an agreement. An invitation only asks people to make offers.'

Checker: Line 12 (voice): 'The reward advertisement is the one exception' is too absolute, and it isn't clear what it is an exception to. Suggested wording: 'Unlike ordinary advertisements, a reward advertisement is a general offer, not an invitation.'
Checker: Line 4 (board flow): the 'to_note=takes price' label is vague. It should show acceptance, e.g. 'to_note=accepts at counter', so the board matches the voice line ('the shopkeeper accepts').
